name: Bupropion
route_note: Oral immediate-, sustained- or extended-release tablets; also in fixed combinations with naltrexone and dextromethorphan.

discovery.note: A cathinone-related aminoketone synthesised during a search for antidepressants without tricyclic side effects.

tagline: Atypical antidepressant and smoking-cessation aid without sexual side effects
summary: Bupropion is an aminoketone antidepressant that inhibits noradrenaline and dopamine reuptake and antagonises nicotinic receptors. It is used for depression, seasonal affective disorder and smoking cessation, and in combinations for obesity and depression. It is notable for not causing sexual dysfunction or weight gain, but it lowers the seizure threshold.
mechanism: Bupropion and its major active metabolite hydroxybupropion weakly inhibit the dopamine and noradrenaline transporters, increasing catecholamine signalling; it has no meaningful serotonergic activity.
Both compounds are non-competitive antagonists of neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, which is thought to contribute to reduced craving and withdrawal during smoking cessation.

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Nariman Mehta synthesises bupropion at Burroughs Wellcome.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Wellbutrin for depression.

history.title: Withdrawal
history.detail: Launch is halted after seizures in bulimic patients at high doses.

history.title: Reintroduction
history.detail: Bupropion returns with lower maximum doses.

history.title: Zyban
history.detail: Sustained-release bupropion is approved for smoking cessation.

history.title: Wellbutrin XL
history.detail: Once-daily extended-release bupropion is approved; seasonal affective disorder follows in 2006.

history.title: Neuropsychiatric boxed warning
history.detail: The FDA adds a boxed warning on neuropsychiatric events for smoking-cessation use.

history.title: Contrave
history.detail: The naltrexone–bupropion combination is approved for weight management.

history.title: Warning removed
history.detail: After the EAGLES trial the neuropsychiatric boxed warning for smoking cessation is removed.

history.title: Auvelity
history.detail: Dextromethorphan–bupropion is approved for major depressive disorder.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP2B6 to hydroxybupropion; strong CYP2D6 inhibitor

safety.boxed_warning: Increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in children, adolescents and young adults (under 25) taking antidepressants; monitor for clinical worsening.

facts: Bupropion is contraindicated in seizure disorders and in bulimia or anorexia nervosa because of seizure risk.
It inhibits CYP2D6 strongly enough to alter doses of many other drugs.
